To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a SCADA system that can tolerate simultaneous intrusions and attacks, that we deployed this SCADA system across three sites over a 250-mile span, and that this deployment delivered 99.9999% of SCADA updates within 100ms of their origination, meeting the latency requirements of the power grid.

we have developed Spire, the world's first intrusion-toleranted SCADA system that meets the latency and availability requirements for the power grid, and we have demonstrated that Spire can deliver nearly 99.99% of all SCAD updates initiated in a wide-area deployment spanning 250 miles in less than 100ms.
Spire is the first intrusion-tolerance SCADA system that can tolerate simultaneous intrusions and attacks on the network and that can meet the latency requirement of the power grid.

building a secure and resilient SCADA system for the power grid.
building intrusion-tolerant systems that can withstand sophisticated attacks, such as those that have been used in recent years to attack the power grid, including those that target control systems.
the design and implementation of a distributed SCADA system that can withstand sophisticated network attacks and simultaneous intrusions.
